ruling.recommended_action: Refer B-0025 to a human reviewer: obtain the vehicle's driven path/road-name trace for 10:13–10:24 and any stop or location records for that window, read F8/F9 against that trace to settle the scope of the rider's "Sure, your call.", and apply RD-5 to F3 before any refund is issued; no account flag is requested.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a RydeTAXI metered trip, so extra kilometres enter the fare: F7 breaks the $46.18 charge into disclosed metered units (base $3.90, distance $31.30 for 22.20 km, time $9.38, waiting $0.13, platform $1.47) and F4 shows the billed excess mileage figure at this trip's rate ($31.30 ÷ 22.20 km = $1.4099/km, as F4 states) [F7][F4][RD-2]. Only one off-route segment exists — F3, 10:13–10:24, 7.21 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.29 km, adding 4.92 km — and the remaining +5.7 km in F1 is corridor-level mismatch RD-2 leaves with the rider [F3][F1][RD-1][RD-2]. The RD-4 traffic screen is closed against the driver by the trace: F15's vehicle breakdown is recorded 0 m from the optimal route at 09:47, but the trace finds no qualifying incident for the 10:13 segment and F12's AYE band-2 window expires at 10:13, when the segment begins, so F12 and F13/F14 (other corridors) cannot exempt it and band evidence cannot stand alone [F15][F12][F13][F14][RD-4]. The driver's own post-trip statement F11 is a statement, not consent, and adds nothing [F11][RD-5].

The case therefore turns on RD-5 and F3 cannot be settled on this record. Before the segment, the driver asked in chat "mind if I go round via Clementi Avenue 2?" at 10:10 (F8) and the rider replied "Sure, your call." at 10:10 (F9), with a complete, timestamped two-message record (F10) — so the timing condition can be met from the record without the driver's statement [F8][F9][F10][RD-5]. But the kind of agreement is squarely contested: the driver reads F9 as a general route choice covering the route taken to Jurong East, the rider reads F8 as naming the alternative road so that F9 is a yes to a named road only [F8][F9][RD-5]. That is exactly the case where no exemption executes on the contested words and the segment must be found undetermined. On the named-road reading the record also fails to tie the segment to Clementi Avenue 2: F10 says the chat has only two messages, no road name appears in F3, and there is no stop or locating fact inside 10:13–10:24, so under RD-5 and G13 (no road-name evidence for the driven path) the finding would be undetermined rather than exempt [F3][F10][RD-5]. Similarly RD-3(a) gives no exemption: no rider message in F8–F9 named any place and no stop is measured in the segment [F8][F9][F3][RD-3].

Because the segment reading is undetermined and the trace states that this finding changes the amount, the case goes to a person, and I rule escalate rather than pick the rider's $6.94 or the driver's no_action [F3][RD-2][RD-5]. No account flag: neither party has an upheld route dispute in 90 days (rider 0/1, driver 0/1), so RD-6's repeated-breach threshold is unmet, and profile facts could not decide the route question anyway [F17][F18][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read every message — F8 (driver's congestion question), F9 (rider's reply), F11 (driver's post-trip breakdown explanation) and the complaint (a fare complaint about a longer route) — and found no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, and no accident or injury in the record [F8][F9][F11][SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. Safety_concern is none on that reading. The blocker is not safety but the record: nothing in the materials places the driven 10:13–10:24 path on any named road (F3 carries no road name, and F10 shows only two chat messages), so the RD-5 scope element cannot be settled [F3][F10][RD-5].
ruling.escalation_reason: segment finding undetermined for F3; evidence insufficient: No record ties the driven off-route path (F3, 10:13–10:24) to any named road or place: F3 carries no road name, F10 shows the chat consists of only two messages, and there is no stop or locating fact within the segment window, so the RD-5 scope of the rider's 10:10 agreement (F9, replying to F8's naming of Clementi Avenue 2) cannot be read from the materials. Without that, the segment's consequence — exempt, counts or undetermined — and therefore the RD-2 amount cannot be settled.

segment_findings.reason: The rider's message F9 'Sure, your call.' (10:10) is a reply to the driver's F8 (10:10) naming an alternative road, Clementi Avenue 2; one side reads F9 as a general route choice and the other as a yes to a named road, so no exemption executes on the contested words and the kind of agreement is undetermined. The record also carries no tie between the F3 driven path (10:13–10:24) and Clementi Avenue 2 — F3 names no road, and F10 shows the chat has only two messages, with no stop or locating message in the segment — which per RD-5 / G13 means the segment is not shown to be the agreed road rather than an agreed route. Timing alone (consent at 10:10 before the 10:13 segment start) satisfies RD-5 but not the scope element. [RD-5][RD-3][RD-2]

rejected_claims.reason: Correct as far as it goes — F3 is the only off-route segment and no RD-4/RD-5 exemption is established — but RD-1 alone does not entitle the rider to a refund; the segment's RD-5 scope is undetermined, so no refund can be computed on this record [F3][F8][F9][RD-1][RD-5].

The $6.94 figure presupposes the F3 segment is unexempted; because the RD-5 reading of F8/F9 is contested and the driven path is not tied to any named road, the segment is undetermined rather than counting, so the amount cannot be computed here [F3][F8][F9][F10][RD-2][RD-5].

'Your call' being at most a general route choice is only one of two argued readings, and general consent would still have to cover this 7.21 km loop reaching no stop; the record does not settle which reading applies, so this claim cannot ground an exemption-side or a counts-side outcome [F3][F8][F9][RD-5].

Accepted that F11 is a post-trip statement and cannot itself exempt, and that F15's breakdown sits on the AYE — the RD-4 screen is settled against the driver by the trace — but that only removes the driver's exemption, it does not make the F3 segment refundable, since the RD-5 element remains unresolved [F11][F15][F12][F3][RD-4][RD-5].

Reading F9 as a general route authorisation is a plausible reading but it is contested by the rider's reading of F8 as naming the alternative road; the record does not settle which kind of agreement was given, so no exemption can execute on it [F8][F9][RD-5].

Correct that no fact places the car on an errand of the driver's own and there is no stop fact in 10:13–10:24, but that does not yield an exemption either: with no road-name tie the segment is undetermined under RD-5/G13, not consented [F3][F9][F10][RD-5].

F15's breakdown is 0 m from the optimal route and predates the segment, but the trace marks RD-4(a) as failed for the 10:13–10:24 off-route segment, and F12's band-2 window ends at 10:13 when the segment begins; band evidence cannot exempt on its own [F15][F12][F3][RD-4].

RD-4(a) does not apply to this segment on the trace, and RD-4(b) band evidence is corroboration only and cannot stand alone, so the requested no_action exemption is not made out; the segment remains undetermined under RD-5 [F15][F12][F3][RD-4][RD-5].

F4's $7.99 on 5.67 km is the whole-trip billed excess, which includes corridor-level mismatch RD-2 leaves with the rider (F1 +5.7 km vs F3 4.92 km); it is a ceiling figure, not the measure of the one off-route segment, so it cannot be used as the RD-2 amount for F3 [F4][F3][F1][RD-2].

Without that, the segment's consequence — exempt, counts or undetermined — and therefore the RD-2 amount cannot be settled.
